answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a small, time-locked stake that is slashed on fraud, with the stake amount rising steeply at the zenith of demand. Reputation should accrue slowly like a pearl forming layer by layer, so a fresh fake identity starts worthless and cannot outvote established agents. A gale of cheap new accounts then buys nothing, because influence is earned through verified work and attested history, not account count.
